$comment: A reference tenant config, with every field the schema understands.
Copy this, rename it after the client, and delete what you do not need —
most of it is optional and the engine has workable defaults. Check your
work with `npm run tenants:check`, which names and locates every problem
rather than stopping at the first.
Two things are worth understanding before editing:
1. MILLIMETRES ARE THE COORDINATE SYSTEM. Nothing declares a texture size.
The studio derives its resolution from `print.physical`, at one density
on both axes, so a print area cannot describe pixels that disagree with
its physical shape. Get the millimetres right and everything else
follows.
2. MOST MODELS NEED `decal`, NOT `texture`. A model authored for print has
flat unrolled UVs, one island per panel, and can use `texture` with a
`uv` window. A model from an asset library almost never does — its UV
atlas was built for a photograph, and often every face shares the same
patch, so artwork applied through it appears on all six sides at once.
Those need `decal`, which projects a print surface onto the panel. Run
`npm run models:uv` to find out which you have.
$comment_assetBase: Where this client's models live. Empty means the page's own origin, which
is right when the host serves them itself. A CDN prefix is the usual
The Draco decoder is NOT here. It is the same wasm for every client and is
served by the host, not from a client's bucket.
$comment_branding: Three colours and a few fonts are enough. The studio derives its ink and
paper ramps from `ink` and `paper`, so a client who supplies little still
gets a coherent result rather than three right colours and forty wrong
`tokens` is the escape hatch, for a brand that is a designed ramp rather
than a rule. It writes CSS custom properties verbatim and wins over
everything above it. Most clients should not need it.

branding.fontArabic: 'IBM Plex Sans Arabic', 'Noto Sans Arabic', sans-serif

$comment_stocks: The board this client actually prints on. A print house does not sell hex
values, it sells stock — so these are named materials with the colour they
come out as, and the studio offers a real choice rather than a colour
wheel. Products name them by the key.
Labels may be one string or a map of locale to string. They are the
client's own words for their own materials, which is why they live here
and not in a translation file.

products.$comment: A product whose model was authored for print: flat unrolled UVs.

model.$comment: Paths are relative to assetBase. Run models:inspect for the names.

camera.$comment: A viewing direction, not a distance. Distance is computed from heightM.

print.$comment_uv: The printable window inside the mesh's UV space. Outside it is bare stock.
$comment_physical: The finished size of the flat print area. safeMm may be one number or
one per edge — per-edge is usually right, since a cup's rim curl eats
print.$comment_dpi: Screen resolution is capped by a texture budget; press resolution is not.
print.$comment_wrap: Left and right edges are the same seam, so artwork crossing one reappears.
print.$comment_defaultTransform: Fractions of the print area, resolved to millimetres on load.

$comment: A product from an asset library, whose UVs are not a print layout.
The studio builds its own print surface by projecting the panel.

$comment_projection: Which way the printed panel faces, in world space after the model's
own rotations. `npm run models:axis` reports it — the front face in
the file is rarely the front face in the scene.
threshold: how square-on a triangle must be to count. Raise it to
keep print off gussets and curves.
inset: fraction held back from the folded edges.
